relationships.subject: neuropeptide Y
relationships.evidence_quote: Neuropeptide Y targets the Y1 receptor (Y1) in the spinal dorsal horn (DH) to produce endogenous and exogenous analgesia.

relationships.subject: [Leu31, Pro34]-NPY
relationships.evidence_quote: [Leu31, Pro34]-NPY reduced SNI-induced allodynia in both control Npy1rloxP/loxP and Npy1rloxP/loxP CckCre mice but not in Npy1rloxP/loxP GrpCre mice

relationships.subject: [Leu31, Pro34]-NPY
relationships.evidence_quote: These results indicate that NPY Y1 agonists inhibit behavioral signs of neuropathic pain by actions at spinal cord Npy1r-expressing interneurons that coexpress Grp but not Cck or Npff.

relationships.subject: spared nerve injury
relationships.evidence_quote: Fos expression was principally expressed in the Grp/Npy1r subpopulation rather than the Npff/Npy1r or Cck/Npy1r subpopulations

relationships.subject: Npff/Npy1r interneurons
relationships.evidence_quote: These findings indicate that spinal Npff/Npy1r-INs are not necessary for the behavioral manifestation of mechanical or cold neuropathic hypersensitivity.

key_findings: Spinal Y1-INs are glutamatergic and segregate into Grp/Npy1r, Npff/Npy1r and Cck/Npy1r subpopulations conserved in mouse, macaque and human dorsal horn.
Intrathecal Y1 agonist [Leu31, Pro34]-NPY reduced SNI-induced allodynia except when Npy1r was deleted from GRP-INs; chemogenetic inhibition of Npff/Npy1r-INs had no effect.
